It’s like burying money and people in the ground: the former head of Take-Two explained why developing modern AAA games is not sustainable
Published by
admin
Tags:
Take-Two
Ben Feder, who led Take-Two Interactive from 2007 to 2011, gave a substantial interview to The Game Business. During the conversation, he
spoke
about the current issues in AAA development.
GTA VI
According to Feder, the game development industry is currently not in the best condition. Studios are closing, employees are being laid off, and the competition for audience attention is rapidly increasing. He sees a silver lining in these events — amidst this turmoil, companies are beginning to adopt new technologies and spend money more wisely. Nevertheless, the former head of Take-Two is convinced that under such conditions, AAA game developers are taking significant risks.
The issue, Feder explains, is that modern AAA games are too massive for their creators to afford to experiment. Yet, they are still too small to transform from mere games into full-fledged platforms.
The situation is worsened by the high cost of production. Feder remarks that major publishers he spoke with do not understand how to make AAA games for less than 300 million dollars. The lengthy development timelines concern the former head of Take-Two just as much.
“Greenlighting a $300 million game that takes five years is as if you’re taking your entire development team, putting them in a time capsule, burying them in the ground, and five years later they pop out and say, ‘Voila, here it is.’ Three to five years ago, that was reasonable because we know what they’re building, it’s good IP, they have a niche, and we know what the world’s going to look like when they pop out of the ground. Today, while they’re underground, on the surface of planet Earth all of this change is happening, not just technologically but also with respect to consumer tastes and expectations. They may come out five years from now, and the world may not care.” stated Feder.
The exception, according to Feder, is GTA VI, as it is indeed capable of transcending ordinary games and approaching platforms. However, replicating its success is extremely difficult: this would require operating with budgets not in the millions, but in the billions of dollars.
